sections.overview: The pied avocet is a black-and-white wader found across parts of Europe, Africa and Asia.
sections.identification: Its long, slender bill curves upward, and its long legs are bluish grey.
sections.habitat: It frequents shallow, open wetlands such as estuaries, mudflats, lagoons and salt pans.
sections.diet: Walking through shallow water, it sweeps its bill from side to side to catch small invertebrates in mud or water.
sections.behavior: Some populations migrate, while others remain in their region year-round.
sections.reproduction: It nests in colonies near water, often on bare ground or in sparse vegetation.
sections.ecology: Its upturned bill is adapted to its distinctive lateral-sweeping feeding method.
sections.conservation: The consulted species accounts classify it as Least Concern.
